findings.reason: without a rule that treats a `launch-failed` pointer as re-queueable, the drainer's stated loop strands exactly the request the paragraph promises it preserves, and done-when bullet 3 ("a launch failure leaves the run queued") cannot be met for the post-spawn case; the node must add that re-queue step to the drainer pass.
findings.text: §4 says the drainer keeps the queued pointer and "on either outcome it writes the pointer back as `queued` … so a failed attempt never destroys the request", but the second outcome it names (a post-spawn failure with no manifest) is marked `launch-failed` by `_record_launch_failure`, which runs in `_reap_launched_workers`/the supervisor, not inside the drainer's dispatch call — and §4's own cadence only "reads the lane document and the queued pointers", so a pointer left in `launch-failed` is never surfaced as queued work

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_release_launch_claim` (dispatch_claims.py:619) and `LAUNCH_FAILED_PHASE`/`launch-failed` (dispatch_launch.py:93) resolve; the shared evidence link `a-held-dispatch-waits-its-fair-turn-landed.html#s2/#s3` resolves to ids present in that file.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §4's four bullets are measurable, and bullets 2 and 3 carry declared negative controls (two racing drainers launch each run once; a paused fleet gate launches nothing), so the guard can be shown to fire.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §4 cites durable repository paths (`reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py`) and names no scratchpad or node-local path; the node's gate log is supplied by the runner.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols are mechanism words (`admit`, `--lane`, `--once`), and the phase words `queued`/`starting`/`working`/`launch-failed` are code vocabulary, not plan labels or ticket numbers.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4 states the drainer restores the pointer "on either outcome", but its cited `launch-failed` marking is written asynchronously by the reaper, so a queued-pointer cadence cannot observe it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — "One drainer launches queued work" is a single deliverable; the admit verb and its temporary-services-config test are the same deliverable's surface, not a second one.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §4's relationships are unchanged (plan-after `the-local-lane-is-the-default`, standalone); nothing §4 relies on is a missing edge.
